metric.label: Lexical baseline
metric.description: Character n-gram cosine distance. This is a reproducible lexical baseline, not a semantic or faithfulness score.

units.leftText: This is the word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and of Jeroboam son of Jehoash, king of Israel.
units.rightText: The word of Jehovah that came unto Hosea the son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.
leftNotes: 1:1 Hebrew Joash, a variant of Jehoash

units.leftText: When the LORD first spoke through Hosea, He told him, “Go, take a prostitute as your wife and have children of adultery, because this land is flagrantly prostituting itself by departing from the LORD.”
units.rightText: When Jehovah spake at the first by Hosea, Jehovah said unto Hosea, Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredom and children of whoredom; for the land doth commit great whoredom, departing from Jehovah.

units.leftText: So Hosea went and married Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.
units.rightText: So he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim; and she conceived, and bare him a son.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Hosea, “Name him Jezreel, for soon I will bring the bloodshed of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and I will put an end to the kingdom of Israel.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto him, Call his name Jezreel; for yet a little while, and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and will cause the kingdom of the house of Israel to cease.
leftNotes: 1:4 Jezreel means God sows; also in verse 11.

units.leftText: And on that day I will break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel.”
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass at that day, that I will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel.

units.leftText: Gomer again conceived and gave birth to a daughter, and the LORD said to Hosea, “Name her Lo-ruhamah, for I will no longer have compassion on the house of Israel, that I should ever forgive them.
units.rightText: And she conceived again, and bare a daughter. And Jehovah said unto him, Call her name Lo-ruhamah; for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel, that I should in any wise pardon them.
leftNotes: 1:6 Lo-ruhamah means she has not received mercy.

units.leftText: Yet I will have compassion on the house of Judah, and I will save them — not by bow or sword or war, not by horses and cavalry, but by the LORD their God.”
units.rightText: But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them by Jehovah their God, and will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen.

units.leftText: After she had weaned Lo-ruhamah, Gomer conceived and gave birth to a son.
units.rightText: Now when she had weaned Lo-ruhamah, she conceived, and bare a son.

units.leftText: And the LORD said, “Name him Lo-ammi, for you are not My people, and I am not your God.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said, Call his name Lo-ammi; for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.
leftNotes: 1:9 Lo-ammi means not My people.
1:9 Hebrew I am not yours

units.leftText: Yet the number of the Israelites will be like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured or counted. And it will happen that in the very place where it was said to them, ‘You are not My people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’
units.rightText: Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass that, in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.
leftNotes: 1:10 Cited in Romans 9:26|ROM 9:26*

units.leftText: Then the people of Judah and of Israel will be gathered together, and they will appoint for themselves one leader, and will go up out of the land. For great will be the day of Jezreel.[’’]
units.rightText: And the children of Judah and the children of Israel shall be gathered together, and they shall appoint themselves one head, and shall go up from the land; for great shall be the day of Jezreel.

units.leftText: “Say of your brothers, ‘My people,’ and of your sisters, ‘My loved one.’
units.rightText: Say ye unto your brethren, Ammi; and to your sisters, Ruhamah.
leftNotes: 2:1 Hebrew Ammi
2:1 Or Mercy is shown; Hebrew Ruhamah, which means she has received mercy

units.leftText: Rebuke your mother, rebuke her, for she is not My wife, and I am not her husband. Let her remove the adultery from her face and the unfaithfulness from between her breasts.
units.rightText: Contend with your mother, contend; for she is not my wife, neither am I her husband; and let her put away her whoredoms from her face, and her adulteries from between her breasts;

units.leftText: Otherwise, I will strip her naked and expose her like the day of her birth. I will make her like a desert and turn her into a parched land, and I will let her die of thirst.
units.rightText: lest I strip her naked, and set her as in the day that she was born, and make her as a wilderness, and set her like a dry land, and slay her with thirst.

units.leftText: I will have no compassion on her children, because they are the children of adultery.
units.rightText: Yea, upon her children will I have no mercy; for they are children of whoredom;

units.leftText: For their mother has played the harlot and has conceived them in disgrace. For she thought, ‘I will go after my lovers, who give me bread and water, wool and linen, oil and drink.’
units.rightText: for their mother hath played the harlot; she that conceived them hath done shamefully; for she said, I will go after my lovers, that give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, mine oil and my drink.

units.leftText: Therefore, behold, I will hedge up her path with thorns; I will enclose her with a wall, so she cannot find her way.
units.rightText: Therefore, behold, I will hedge up thy way with thorns, and I will build a wall against her, that she shall not find her paths.
leftNotes: 2:6 Hebrew your path

units.leftText: She will pursue her lovers but not catch them; she will seek them but not find them. Then she will say, ‘I will return to my first husband, for then I was better off than now.’
units.rightText: And she shall follow after her lovers, but she shall not overtake them; and she shall seek them, but shall not find them: then shall she say, I will go and return to my first husband; for then was it better with me than now.

units.leftText: For she does not acknowledge that it was I who gave her grain, new wine, and oil, who lavished on her silver and gold — which they crafted for Baal.
units.rightText: For she did not know that I gave her the grain, and the new wine, and the oil, and multiplied unto her silver and gold, which they used for Baal.

units.leftText: Therefore I will take back My grain in its time and My new wine in its season; I will take away My wool and linen, which were given to cover her nakedness.
units.rightText: Therefore will I take back my grain in the time thereof, and my new wine in the season thereof, and will pluck away my wool and my flax which should have covered her nakedness.

units.leftText: And then I will expose her lewdness in the sight of her lovers, and no one will deliver her out of My hands.
units.rightText: And now will I uncover her lewdness in the sight of her lovers, and none shall deliver her out of my hand.

units.leftText: I will put an end to all her exultation: her feasts, New Moons, and Sabbaths— all her appointed feasts.
units.rightText: I will also cause all her mirth to cease, her feasts, her new moons, and her sabbaths, and all her solemn assemblies.

units.leftText: I will destroy her vines and fig trees, which she thinks are the wages paid by her lovers. So I will make them into a thicket, and the beasts of the field will devour them.
units.rightText: And I will lay waste her vines and her fig-trees, whereof she hath said, These are my hire that my lovers have given me; and I will make them a forest, and the beasts of the field shall eat them.

units.leftText: I will punish her for the days of the Baals when she burned incense to them, when she adorned herself with rings and jewelry, and went after her lovers. But Me she forgot,” declares the LORD. God’s Mercy to Israel
units.rightText: And I will visit upon her the days of the Baalim, unto which she burned incense, when she decked herself with her earrings and her jewels, and went after her lovers, and forgat me, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “Therefore, behold, I will allure her and lead her to the wilderness, and speak to her tenderly.
units.rightText: Therefore, behold, I will allure her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak comfortably unto her.

units.leftText: There I will give back her vineyards and make the Valley of Achor into a gateway of hope. There she will respond as she did in the days of her youth, as in the day she came up out of Egypt.
units.rightText: And I will give her her vineyards from thence, and the valley of Achor for a door of hope; and she shall make answer there, as in the days of her youth, and as in the day when she came up out of the land of Egypt.
leftNotes: 2:15 Achor means trouble.

units.leftText: In that day,” declares the LORD, “you will call Me ‘my Husband,’ and no longer call Me ‘my Master.’
units.rightText: And it shall be at that day, saith Jehovah, that thou shalt call me Ishi, and shalt call me no more Baali.
leftNotes: 2:16 Hebrew my Ishi
2:16 Hebrew my Baal

units.leftText: For I will remove from her lips the names of the Baals; no longer will their names be invoked.
units.rightText: For I will take away the names of the Baalim out of her mouth, and they shall no more be mentioned by their name.

units.leftText: On that day I will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air and the creatures that crawl on the ground. And I will abolish bow and sword and battle in the land, and will make them lie down in safety.
units.rightText: And in that day will I make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field, and with the birds of the heavens, and with the creeping things of the ground: and I will break the bow and the sword and the battle out of the land, and will make them to lie down safely.

units.leftText: So I will betroth you to Me forever; I will betroth you in righteousness and justice, in loving devotion and compassion.
units.rightText: And I will betroth thee unto me for ever; yea, I will betroth thee unto me in righteousness, and in justice, and in lovingkindness, and in mercies.
leftNotes: 2:19 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: And I will betroth you in faithfulness, and you will know the LORD.”
units.rightText: I will even betroth thee unto me in faithfulness; and thou shalt know Jehovah.

units.leftText: “On that day I will respond —” declares the LORD — “I will respond to the heavens, and they will respond to the earth.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, I will answer, saith Jehovah, I will answer the heavens, and they shall answer the earth;

units.leftText: And the earth will respond to the grain, to the new wine and oil, and they will respond to Jezreel.
units.rightText: and the earth shall answer the grain, and the new wine, and the oil; and they shall answer Jezreel.
leftNotes: 2:22 Jezreel means God sows.

units.leftText: And I will sow her as My own in the land, and I will have compassion on ‘No Compassion.’ I will say to those called ‘Not My People,’ ‘You are My people,’ and they will say, ‘You are my God.’”
units.rightText: And I will sow her unto me in the earth; and I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to them that were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my God.
leftNotes: 2:23 Hebrew Lo-ruhamah; LXX I will love her who was not loved
2:23 Hebrew Lo-ammi
2:23 Cited in Romans 9:25|ROM 9:25* and 1 Peter 2:10

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to me, “Go show love to your wife again, though she is loved by another and is an adulteress. Love her as the LORD loves the Israelites, though they turn to other gods and love to offer raisin cakes to idols. ”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto me, Go again, love a woman beloved of her friend, and an adulteress, even as Jehovah loveth the children of Israel, though they turn unto other gods, and love cakes of raisins.
leftNotes: 3:1 Or Go show love to a woman who is loved by another
3:1 Literally and love raisin cakes

units.leftText: So I bought her for fifteen shekels of silver and a homer and a lethech of barley.
units.rightText: So I bought her to me for fifteen pieces of silver, and a homer of barley, and a half-homer of barley;
leftNotes: 3:2 15 shekels is approximately 6 ounces or 171 grams of silver.

3:2 Or a homer and a half of barley; that is, a total of approximately 9.36 bushels or 330 liters (probably about 436 pounds or 198 kilograms of barley); LXX a homer of barley and a wineskin full of wine

units.leftText: Then I said to her, “You must live with me for many days; you must not be promiscuous or belong to another, and I will do the same for you.”
units.rightText: and I said unto her, Thou shalt abide for me many days; thou shalt not play the harlot, and thou shalt not be any man’s wife: so will I also be toward thee.

units.leftText: For the Israelites must live many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or sacred pillar, and without ephod or idol.
units.rightText: For the children of Israel shall abide many days without king, and without prince, and without sacrifice, and without pillar, and without ephod or teraphim:

units.leftText: Afterward, the people of Israel will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king. They will come trembling to the LORD and to His goodness in the last days.
units.rightText: afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek Jehovah their God, and David their king, and shall come with fear unto Jehovah and to his goodness in the latter days.

units.leftText: Hear the word of the LORD, O children of Israel, for the LORD has a case against the people of the land: “There is no truth, no loving devotion, and no knowledge of God in the land!
units.rightText: Hear the word of Jehovah, ye children of Israel; for Jehovah hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor goodness, nor knowledge of God in the land.

units.leftText: Cursing and lying, murder and stealing, and adultery are rampant; one act of bloodshed follows another.
units.rightText: There is nought but swearing and breaking faith, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery; they break out, and blood toucheth blood.

units.leftText: Therefore the land mourns, and all who dwell in it will waste away with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air; even the fish of the sea disappear.
units.rightText: Therefore shall the land mourn, and every one that dwelleth therein shall languish, with the beasts of the field and the birds of the heavens; yea, the fishes of the sea also shall be taken away.

units.leftText: But let no man contend; let no man offer reproof; for your people are like those who contend with a priest.
units.rightText: Yet let no man strive, neither let any man reprove; for thy people are as they that strive with the priest.
leftNotes: 4:4 Or for My case is against you, O priests

units.leftText: You will stumble by day, and the prophet will stumble with you by night; so I will destroy your mother —
units.rightText: And thou shalt stumble in the day, and the prophet also shall stumble with thee in the night; and I will destroy thy mother.

units.leftText: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I will also reject you as My priests. Since you have forgotten the law of your God, I will also forget your children.
units.rightText: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I also will forget thy children.

units.leftText: The more they multiplied, the more they sinned against Me; they exchanged their Glory for a thing of disgrace.
units.rightText: As they were multiplied, so they sinned against me: I will change their glory into shame.
leftNotes: 4:7 Or they exchanged their glorious God (Syriac); MT I will exchange their glory

units.leftText: They feed on the sins of My people and set their hearts on iniquity.
units.rightText: They feed on the sin of my people, and set their heart on their iniquity.
leftNotes: 4:8 Or the sin offerings

units.leftText: And it shall be like people, like priest. I will punish both of them for their ways and repay them for their deeds.
units.rightText: And it shall be, like people, like priest; and I will punish them for their ways, and will requite them their doings.

units.leftText: They will eat but not be satisfied; they will be promiscuous but not multiply. For they have abandoned the LORD to give themselves
units.rightText: And they shall eat, and not have enough; they shall play the harlot, and shall not increase; because they have left off taking heed to Jehovah.

units.leftText: to promiscuity, wine, and new wine, which take away understanding.
units.rightText: Whoredom and wine and new wine take away the understanding.

units.leftText: My people consult their wooden idols, and their divining rods inform them. For a spirit of prostitution leads them astray and they have played the harlot against their God.
units.rightText: My people ask counsel at their stock, and their staff declareth unto them; for the spirit of whoredom hath caused them to err, and they have played the harlot, departing from under their God.

units.leftText: They sacrifice on the mountaintops and burn offerings on the hills, under oak, poplar, and terebinth, because their shade is pleasant. And so your daughters turn to prostitution and your daughters-in-law to adultery.
units.rightText: They sacrifice upon the tops of the mountains, and burn incense upon the hills, under oaks and poplars and terebinths, because the shadow thereof is good: therefore your daughters play the harlot, and your brides commit adultery.

units.leftText: I will not punish your daughters when they prostitute themselves, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery. For the men themselves go off with prostitutes and offer sacrifices with shrine prostitutes. So a people without understanding will come to ruin.
units.rightText: I will not punish your daughters when they play the harlot, nor your brides when they commit adultery; for the men themselves go apart with harlots, and they sacrifice with the prostitutes; and the people that doth not understand shall be overthrown.

units.leftText: Though you prostitute yourself, O Israel, may Judah avoid such guilt! Do not journey to Gilgal, do not go up to Beth-aven, and do not swear on oath, ‘As surely as the LORD lives!’
units.rightText: Though thou, Israel, play the harlot, yet let not Judah offend; and come not ye unto Gilgal, neither go ye up to Beth-aven, nor swear, As Jehovah liveth.
leftNotes: 4:15 Beth-aven means house of wickedness. This is a derogatory term for Bethel, which means house of God; see 1 Kings 12:28–29|1KI 12:28-29*.

units.leftText: For Israel is as obstinate as a stubborn heifer. Can the LORD now shepherd them like lambs in an open meadow?
units.rightText: For Israel hath behaved himself stubbornly, like a stubborn heifer: now will Jehovah feed them as a lamb in a large place.

units.leftText: Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone!
units.rightText: Ephraim is joined to idols; let him alone.
leftNotes: 4:17 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel

units.leftText: When their liquor is gone, they turn to prostitution; their rulers dearly love disgrace.
units.rightText: Their drink is become sour; they play the harlot continually; her rulers dearly love shame.
leftNotes: 4:18 Hebrew her shields

units.leftText: The whirlwind has wrapped them in its wings, and their sacrifices will bring them shame.[’’]
units.rightText: The wind hath wrapped her up in its wings; and they shall be put to shame because of their sacrifices.
leftNotes: 4:19 Hebrew has wrapped her

units.leftText: “Hear this, O priests! Take heed, O house of Israel! Give ear, O royal house! For this judgment is against you because you have been a snare at Mizpah, a net spread out on Tabor.
units.rightText: Hear this, O ye priests, and hearken, O house of Israel, and give ear, O house of the king; for unto you pertaineth the judgment; for ye have been a snare at Mizpah, and a net spread upon Tabor.

units.leftText: The rebels are deep in slaughter; but I will chastise them all.
units.rightText: And the revolters are gone deep in making slaughter; but I am a rebuker of them all.

units.leftText: I know all about Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from Me. For now, O Ephraim, you have turned to prostitution; Israel is defiled.
units.rightText: I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hid from me; for now, O Ephraim, thou hast played the harlot, Israel is defiled.
leftNotes: 5:3 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verses 5, 9, 11, 12, 13, and 14

units.leftText: Their deeds do not permit them to return to their God, for a spirit of prostitution is within them, and they do not know the LORD.
units.rightText: Their doings will not suffer them to turn unto their God; for the spirit of whoredom is within them, and they know not Jehovah.

units.leftText: Israel’s arrogance testifies against them; Israel and Ephraim stumble in their iniquity; even Judah stumbles with them.
units.rightText: And the pride of Israel doth testify to his face: therefore Israel and Ephraim shall stumble in their iniquity; Judah also shall stumble with them.

units.leftText: They go with their flocks and herds to seek the LORD, but they do not find Him; He has withdrawn Himself from them.
units.rightText: They shall go with their flocks and with their herds to seek Jehovah; but they shall not find him: he hath withdrawn himself from them.

units.leftText: They have been unfaithful to the LORD; for they have borne illegitimate children. Now the New Moon will devour them along with their land.
units.rightText: They have dealt treacherously against Jehovah; for they have borne strange children: now shall the new moon devour them with their fields.
leftNotes: 5:7 Or their New Moon feast or the coming month

units.leftText: Blow the ram’s horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah; raise the battle cry in Beth-aven: Lead on, O Benjamin!
units.rightText: Blow ye the cornet in Gibeah, and the trumpet in Ramah: sound an alarm at Beth-aven; behind thee, O Benjamin.
leftNotes: 5:8 Beth-aven means house of wickedness. This is a derogatory term for Bethel, which means house of God; see 1 Kings 12:28–29|1KI 12:28-29*.

units.leftText: Ephraim will be laid waste on the day of rebuke. Among the tribes of Israel I proclaim what is certain.
units.rightText: Ephraim shall become a desolation in the day of rebuke: among the tribes of Israel have I made known that which shall surely be.

units.leftText: The princes of Judah are like those who move boundary stones; I will pour out My fury upon them like water.
units.rightText: The princes of Judah are like them that remove the landmark: I will pour out my wrath upon them like water.
leftNotes: 5:10 See Proverbs 22:28|PRO 22:28* and Proverbs 23:10.

units.leftText: Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment, for he is determined to follow worthless idols.
units.rightText: Ephraim is oppressed, he is crushed in judgment; because he was content to walk after man’s command.
leftNotes: 5:11 Or to follow human precepts

units.leftText: So I am like a moth to Ephraim, and like decay to the house of Judah.
units.rightText: Therefore am I unto Ephraim as a moth, and to the house of Judah as rottenness.

units.leftText: When Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah his wound, then Ephraim turned to Assyria and sent to the great king. But he cannot cure you or heal your wound.
units.rightText: When Ephraim saw his sickness, and Judah saw his wound, then went Ephraim to Assyria, and sent to king Jareb: but he is not able to heal you, neither will he cure you of your wound.
leftNotes: 5:13 Or to King Jareb

units.leftText: For I am like a lion to Ephraim and like a young lion to the house of Judah. I, even I, will tear them to pieces and then go away. I will carry them off where no one can rescue them.
units.rightText: For I will be unto Ephraim as a lion, and as a young lion to the house of Judah: I, even I, will tear and go away; I will carry off, and there shall be none to deliver.

units.leftText: Then I will return to My place until they admit their guilt and seek My face; in their affliction they will earnestly seek Me.”
units.rightText: I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me earnestly.

units.leftText: Come, let us return to the LORD. For He has torn us to pieces, but He will heal us; He has wounded us, but He will bind up our wounds.
units.rightText: Come, and let us return unto Jehovah; for he hath torn, and he will heal us; he hath smitten, and he will bind us up.

units.leftText: After two days He will revive us; on the third day He will raise us up, that we may live in His presence.
units.rightText: After two days will he revive us: on the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live before him.

units.leftText: So let us know — let us press on to know the LORD. As surely as the sun rises, He will appear; He will come to us like the rain, like the spring showers that water the earth.
units.rightText: And let us know, let us follow on to know Jehovah: his going forth is sure as the morning; and he will come unto us as the rain, as the latter rain that watereth the earth.

units.leftText: What shall I do with you, O Ephraim ? What shall I do with you, O Judah? For your loyalty is like a morning mist, like the early dew that vanishes.
units.rightText: O Ephraim, what shall I do unto thee? O Judah, what shall I do unto thee? for your goodness is as a morning cloud, and as the dew that goeth early away.
leftNotes: 6:4 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verse 10

units.leftText: Therefore I have hewn them by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of My mouth, and My judgments go forth like lightning.
units.rightText: Therefore have I hewed them by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of my mouth: and thy judgments are as the light that goeth forth.

units.leftText: For I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
units.rightText: For I desire goodness, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt-offerings.
leftNotes: 6:6 Cited in Matthew 9:13|MAT 9:13* and Matthew 12:7

units.leftText: But they, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant; there they were unfaithful to Me.
units.rightText: But they like Adam have transgressed the covenant: there have they dealt treacherously against me.
leftNotes: 6:7 Or As at Adam, they have transgressed

units.leftText: Gilead is a city of evildoers, tracked with footprints of blood.
units.rightText: Gilead is a city of them that work iniquity; it is stained with blood.

units.leftText: Like raiders who lie in ambush, so does a band of priests; they murder on the way to Shechem; surely they have committed atrocities.
units.rightText: And as troops of robbers wait for a man, so the company of priests murder in the way toward Shechem; yea, they have committed lewdness.

units.leftText: In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing: Ephraim practices prostitution there, and Israel is defiled.
units.rightText: In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing: there whoredom is found in Ephraim, Israel is defiled.

units.leftText: Also for you, O Judah, a harvest is appointed, when I restore My people from captivity.
units.rightText: Also, O Judah, there is a harvest appointed for thee, when I bring back the captivity of my people.
leftNotes: 6:11 Or restore the fortunes of My people

units.leftText: When I heal Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim will be exposed, as well as the crimes of Samaria. For they practice deceit and thieves break in; bandits raid in the streets.
units.rightText: When I would heal Israel, then is the iniquity of Ephraim uncovered, and the wickedness of Samaria; for they commit falsehood, and the thief entereth in, and the troop of robbers ravageth without.
leftNotes: 7:1 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verses 8 and 11

units.leftText: But they fail to consider in their hearts that I remember all their evil. Now their deeds are all around them; they are before My face.
units.rightText: And they consider not in their hearts that I remember all their wickedness: now have their own doings beset them about; they are before my face.

units.leftText: They delight the king with their evil, and the princes with their lies.
units.rightText: They make the king glad with their wickedness, and the princes with their lies.

units.leftText: They are all adulterers, like an oven heated by a baker who needs not stoke the fire from the kneading to the rising of the dough.
units.rightText: They are all adulterers; they are as an oven heated by the baker; he ceaseth to stir the fire, from the kneading of the dough, until it be leavened.

units.leftText: The princes are inflamed with wine on the day of our king; so he joins hands with those who mock him.
units.rightText: On the day of our king the princes made themselves sick with the heat of wine; he stretched out his hand with scoffers.

units.leftText: For they prepare their heart like an oven while they lie in wait; all night their anger smolders; in the morning it blazes like a flaming fire.
units.rightText: For they have made ready their heart like an oven, while they lie in wait: their baker sleepeth all the night; in the morning it burneth as a flaming fire.
leftNotes: 7:6 Literally their baker sleeps

units.leftText: All of them are hot as an oven, and they devour their rulers. All their kings fall; not one of them calls upon Me.
units.rightText: They are all hot as an oven, and devour their judges; all their kings are fallen: there is none among them that calleth unto me.

units.leftText: Ephraim mixes with the nations; Ephraim is an unturned cake.
units.rightText: Ephraim, he mixeth himself among the peoples; Ephraim is a cake not turned.

units.leftText: Foreigners consume his strength, but he does not notice. Even his hair is streaked with gray, but he does not know.
units.rightText: Strangers have devoured his strength, and he knoweth it not: yea, gray hairs are here and there upon him, and he knoweth it not.

units.leftText: Israel’s arrogance testifies against them, yet they do not return to the LORD their God; despite all this, they do not seek Him.
units.rightText: And the pride of Israel doth testify to his face: yet they have not returned unto Jehovah their God, nor sought him, for all this.

units.leftText: So Ephraim has become like a silly, senseless dove — calling out to Egypt, then turning to Assyria.
units.rightText: And Ephraim is like a silly dove, without understanding: they call unto Egypt, they go to Assyria.

units.leftText: As they go, I will spread My net over them; I will bring them down like birds of the air. I will chastise them when I hear them flocking together.
units.rightText: When they shall go, I will spread my net upon them; I will bring them down as the birds of the heavens; I will chastise them, as their congregation hath heard.
leftNotes: 7:12 Or I will chastise them according to what was reported against them in the assembly.

units.leftText: Woe to them, for they have strayed from Me! Destruction to them, for they have rebelled against Me! Though I would redeem them, they speak lies against Me.
units.rightText: Woe unto them! for they have wandered from me; destruction unto them! for they have trespassed against me: though I would redeem them, yet they have spoken lies against me.

units.leftText: They do not cry out to Me from their hearts when they wail upon their beds. They slash themselves for grain and new wine, but turn away from Me.
units.rightText: And they have not cried unto me with their heart, but they howl upon their beds: they assemble themselves for grain and new wine; they rebel against me.
leftNotes: 7:14 Some Hebrew manuscripts and LXX; see 1 Kings 18:28|1KI 18:28*. Most Hebrew manuscripts They gather together

units.leftText: Although I trained and strengthened their arms, they plot evil against Me.
units.rightText: Though I have taught and strengthened their arms, yet do they devise mischief against me.

units.leftText: They turn, but not to the Most High; they are like a faulty bow. Their leaders will fall by the sword for the cursing of their tongue; for this they will be ridiculed in the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: They return, but not to him that is on high; they are like a deceitful bow; their princes shall fall by the sword for the rage of their tongue: this shall be their derision in the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: Put the ram’s horn to your lips! An eagle looms over the house of the LORD, because the people have transgressed My covenant and rebelled against My law.
units.rightText: Set the trumpet to thy mouth. As an eagle he cometh against the house of Jehovah, because they have transgressed my covenant, and trespassed against my law.

units.leftText: Israel cries out to Me, “O our God, we know You!”
units.rightText: They shall cry unto me, My God, we Israel know thee.

units.leftText: But Israel has rejected good; an enemy will pursue him.
units.rightText: Israel hath cast off that which is good: the enemy shall pursue him.

units.leftText: They set up kings, but not by Me. They make princes, but without My approval. With their silver and gold they make themselves idols, to their own destruction.
units.rightText: They have set up kings, but not by me; they have made princes, and I knew it not: of their silver and their gold have they made them idols, that they may be cut off.

units.leftText: He has rejected your calf, O Samaria. My anger burns against them. How long will they be incapable of innocence?
units.rightText: He hath cast off thy calf, O Samaria; mine anger is kindled against them: how long will it be ere they attain to innocency?
leftNotes: 8:5 Or calf idol; see 1 Kings 12:29|1KI 12:29*.

units.leftText: For this thing is from Israel— a craftsman made it, and it is not God. It will be broken to pieces, that calf of Samaria.
units.rightText: For from Israel is even this; the workman made it, and it is no God; yea, the calf of Samaria shall be broken in pieces.

units.leftText: For they sow the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind. There is no standing grain; what sprouts fails to yield flour. Even if it should produce, the foreigners would swallow it up.
units.rightText: For they sow the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind: he hath no standing grain; the blade shall yield no meal; if so be it yield, strangers shall swallow it up.

units.leftText: Israel is swallowed up! Now they are among the nations like a worthless vessel.
units.rightText: Israel is swallowed up: now are they among the nations as a vessel wherein none delighteth.

units.leftText: For they have gone up to Assyria like a wild donkey on its own. Ephraim has hired lovers.
units.rightText: For they are gone up to Assyria, like a wild ass alone by himself: Ephraim hath hired lovers.
leftNotes: 8:9 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verse 11

units.leftText: Though they hire allies among the nations, I will now round them up, and they will begin to diminish under the oppression of the king of princes.
units.rightText: Yea, though they hire among the nations, now will I gather them; and they begin to be diminished by reason of the burden of the king of princes.

units.leftText: Though Ephraim multiplied the altars for sin, they became his altars for sinning.
units.rightText: Because Ephraim hath multiplied altars for sinning, altars have been unto him for sinning.

units.leftText: Though I wrote for them the great things of My law, they regarded them as something strange.
units.rightText: I wrote for him the ten thousand things of my law; but they are counted as a strange thing.

units.leftText: Though they offer sacrifices as gifts to Me, and though they eat the meat, the LORD does not accept them. Now He will remember their iniquity and punish their sins: They will return to Egypt.
units.rightText: As for the sacrifices of mine offerings, they sacrifice flesh and eat it; but Jehovah accepteth them not: now will he remember their iniquity, and visit their sins; they shall return to Egypt.

units.leftText: Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces; Judah has multiplied its fortified cities. But I will send fire upon their cities, and it will consume their citadels.
units.rightText: For Israel hath forgotten his Maker, and builded palaces; and Judah hath multiplied fortified cities: but I will send a fire upon his cities, and it shall devour the castles thereof.

units.leftText: Do not rejoice, O Israel, with exultation like the nations, for you have played the harlot against your God; you have made love for hire on every threshing floor.
units.rightText: Rejoice not, O Israel, for joy, like the peoples; for thou hast played the harlot, departing from thy God; thou hast loved hire upon every grain-floor.

units.leftText: The threshing floor and winepress will not feed them, and the new wine will fail them.
units.rightText: The threshing-floor and the winepress shall not feed them, and the new wine shall fail her.

units.leftText: They will not remain in the land of the LORD; Ephraim will return to Egypt and eat unclean food in Assyria.
units.rightText: They shall not dwell in Jehovah’s land; but Ephraim shall return to Egypt, and they shall eat unclean food in Assyria.
leftNotes: 9:3 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; similarly in verses 8, 11, 13, and 16

units.leftText: They will not pour out wine offerings to the LORD, and their sacrifices will not please Him, but will be to them like the bread of mourners; all who eat will be defiled. For their bread will be for themselves; it will not enter the house of the LORD.
units.rightText: They shall not pour out wine- offerings to Jehovah, neither shall they be pleasing unto him: their sacrifices shall be unto them as the bread of mourners; all that eat thereof shall be polluted; for their bread shall be for their appetite; it shall not come into the house of Jehovah.

units.leftText: What will you do on the appointed day, on the day of the LORD’s feast?
units.rightText: What will ye do in the day of solemn assembly, and in the day of the feast of Jehovah?

units.leftText: For even if they flee destruction, Egypt will gather them and Memphis will bury them. Their precious silver will be taken over by thistles, and thorns will overrun their tents.
units.rightText: For, lo, they are gone away from destruction; yet Egypt shall gather them up, Memphis shall bury them; their pleasant things of silver, nettles shall possess them; thorns shall be in their tents.

units.leftText: The days of punishment have come; the days of retribution have arrived — let Israel know it. The prophet is called a fool, and the inspired man insane, because of the greatness of your iniquity and hostility.
units.rightText: The days of visitation are come, the days of recompense are come; Israel shall know it: the prophet is a fool, the man that hath the spirit is mad, for the abundance of thine iniquity, and because the enmity is great.

units.leftText: The prophet is Ephraim’s watchman, along with my God, yet the snare of the fowler lies on all his paths. Hostility is in the house of his God!
units.rightText: Ephraim was a watchman with my God: as for the prophet, a fowler’s snare is in all his ways, and enmity in the house of his God.
leftNotes: 9:8 Or The prophet is the watchman over Ephraim, the people of my God

units.leftText: They have deeply corrupted themselves as in the days of Gibeah; He will remember their guilt; He will punish their sins.
units.rightText: They have deeply corrupted themselves, as in the days of Gibeah: he will remember their iniquity, he will visit their sins.

units.leftText: I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness. I saw your fathers as the firstfruits of the fig tree in its first season. But they went to Baal-peor, and consecrated themselves to Shame; so they became as detestable as the thing they loved.
units.rightText: I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness; I saw your fathers as the first-ripe in the fig-tree at its first season: but they came to Baal-peor, and consecrated themselves unto the shameful thing, and became abominable like that which they loved.

units.leftText: Ephraim’s glory will fly away like a bird, with no birth, no pregnancy, and no conception.
units.rightText: As for Ephraim, their glory shall fly away like a bird: there shall be no birth, and none with child, and no conception.

units.leftText: Even if they raise their children, I will bereave them of each one. Yes, woe be to them when I turn away from them!
units.rightText: Though they bring up their children, yet will I bereave them, so that not a man shall be left: yea, woe also to them when I depart from them!

units.leftText: I have seen Ephraim, like Tyre, planted in a meadow. But Ephraim will bring out his children for slaughter.
units.rightText: Ephraim, like as I have seen Tyre, is planted in a pleasant place: but Ephraim shall bring out his children to the slayer.

units.leftText: Give them, O LORD— what will You give? Give them wombs that miscarry and breasts that dry up!
units.rightText: Give them, O Jehovah—what wilt thou give? give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.

units.leftText: All their evil appears at Gilgal, for there I hated them. I will drive them from My house for the wickedness of their deeds. I will no longer love them; all their leaders are rebellious.
units.rightText: All their wickedness is in Gilgal; for there I hated them: because of the wickedness of their doings I will drive them out of my house; I will love them no more; all their princes are revolters.

units.leftText: Ephraim is struck down; their root is withered; they cannot bear fruit. Even if they bear children, I will slay the darlings of their wombs.
units.rightText: Ephraim is smitten, their root is dried up, they shall bear no fruit: yea, though they bring forth, yet will I slay the beloved fruit of their womb.

units.leftText: My God will reject them because they have not obeyed Him; and they shall be wanderers among the nations.
units.rightText: My God will cast them away, because they did not hearken unto him; and they shall be wanderers among the nations.

units.leftText: Israel was a luxuriant vine, yielding fruit for himself. The more his fruit increased, the more he increased the altars. The better his land produced, the better he made the sacred pillars.
units.rightText: Israel is a luxuriant vine, that putteth forth his fruit: according to the abundance of his fruit he hath multiplied his altars; according to the goodness of their land they have made goodly pillars.

units.leftText: Their hearts are devious; now they must bear their guilt. The LORD will break down their altars and demolish their sacred pillars.
units.rightText: Their heart is divided; now shall they be found guilty: he will smite their altars, he will destroy their pillars.

units.leftText: Surely now they will say, “We have no king, for we do not revere the LORD. What can a king do for us?”
units.rightText: Surely now shall they say, We have no king; for we fear not Jehovah; and the king, what can he do for us?

units.leftText: They speak mere words; with false oaths they make covenants. So judgment springs up like poisonous weeds in the furrows of a field.
units.rightText: They speak vain words, swearing falsely in making covenants: therefore judgment springeth up as hemlock in the furrows of the field.

units.leftText: The people of Samaria will fear for the calf of Beth-aven. Indeed, its people will mourn over it with its idolatrous priests — those who rejoiced in its glory — for it has been taken from them into exile.
units.rightText: The inhabitants of Samaria shall be in terror for the calves of Beth-aven; for the people thereof shall mourn over it, and the priests thereof that rejoiced over it, for the glory thereof, because it is departed from it.
leftNotes: 10:5 Beth-aven means house of wickedness. This is a derogatory term for Bethel, which means house of God; see 1 Kings 12:28–29|1KI 12:28-29*.

units.leftText: Yes, it will be carried to Assyria as tribute to the great king. Ephraim will be seized with shame; Israel will be ashamed of its wooden idols.
units.rightText: It also shall be carried unto Assyria for a present to king Jareb: Ephraim shall receive shame, and Israel shall be ashamed of his own counsel.
leftNotes: 10:6 Or to King Jareb
10:6 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verse 11
10:6 Or of its own counsel

units.leftText: Samaria will be carried off with her king like a twig on the surface of the water.
units.rightText: As for Samaria, her king is cut off, as foam upon the water.

units.leftText: The high places of Aven will be destroyed— it is the sin of Israel; thorns and thistles will overgrow their altars. Then they will say to the mountains, “Cover us!” and to the hills, “Fall on us!”
units.rightText: The high places also of Aven, the sin of Israel, shall be destroyed: the thorn and the thistle shall come up on their altars; and they shall say to the mountains, Cover us; and to the hills, Fall on us.
leftNotes: 10:8 Or of wickedness; Aven is a reference to Beth-aven (a derogatory term for Bethel); see verse 5.
10:8 Cited in Luke 23:30|LUK 23:30*; see also Revelation 6:16.

units.leftText: Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned, O Israel, and there you have remained. Did not the battle in Gibeah overtake the sons of iniquity?
units.rightText: O Israel, thou hast sinned from the days of Gibeah: there they stood; the battle against the children of iniquity doth not overtake them in Gibeah.
leftNotes: 10:9 Or Did not the battle overtake the sons of iniquity in Gibeah?

units.leftText: I will chasten them when I please; nations will be gathered against them to put them in bondage for their double transgression.
units.rightText: When it is my desire, I will chastise them; and the peoples shall be gathered against them, when they are bound to their two transgressions.

units.leftText: Ephraim is a well-trained heifer that loves to thresh; but I will place a yoke on her fair neck. I will harness Ephraim, Judah will plow, and Jacob will break the hard ground.
units.rightText: And Ephraim is a heifer that is taught, that loveth to tread out the grain; but I have passed over upon her fair neck: I will set a rider on Ephraim; Judah shall plow, Jacob shall break his clods.

units.leftText: Sow for yourselves righteousness and reap the fruit of loving devotion; break up your unplowed ground. For it is time to seek the LORD until He comes and sends righteousness upon you like rain.
units.rightText: Sow to yourselves in righteousness, reap according to kindness; break up your fallow ground; for it is time to seek Jehovah, till he come and rain righteousness upon you.

units.leftText: You have plowed wickedness and reaped injustice; you have eaten the fruit of lies. Because you have trusted in your own way and in the multitude of your mighty men,
units.rightText: Ye have plowed wickedness, ye have reaped iniquity; ye have eaten the fruit of lies; for thou didst trust in thy way, in the multitude of thy mighty men.

units.leftText: the roar of battle will rise against your people, so that all your fortresses will be demolished as Shalman devastated Beth-arbel in the day of battle, when mothers were dashed to pieces along with their children.
units.rightText: Therefore shall a tumult arise among thy people, and all thy fortresses shall be destroyed, as Shalman destroyed Beth-arbel in the day of battle: the mother was dashed in pieces with her children.

units.leftText: Thus it will be done to you, O Bethel, because of your great wickedness. When the day dawns, the king of Israel will be utterly cut off.
units.rightText: So shall Beth-el do unto you because of your great wickedness: at daybreak shall the king of Israel be utterly cut off.

units.leftText: When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called My son.
units.rightText: When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.
leftNotes: 11:1 Cited in Matthew 2:15|MAT 2:15*

units.leftText: But the more I called Israel, the farther they departed from Me. They sacrificed to the Baals and burned incense to carved images.
units.rightText: The more the prophets called them, the more they went from them: they sacrificed unto the Baalim, and burned incense to graven images.
leftNotes: 11:2 LXX; Hebrew The more they called them, the more they went from them.

units.leftText: It was I who taught Ephraim to walk, taking them by the arms, but they never realized that it was I who healed them.
units.rightText: Yet I taught Ephraim to walk; I took them on my arms; but they knew not that I healed them.
leftNotes: 11:3 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verses 8, 9, and 12

units.leftText: I led them with cords of kindness, with ropes of love; I lifted the yoke from their necks and bent down to feed them.
units.rightText: I drew them with cords of a man, with bands of love; and I was to them as they that lift up the yoke on their jaws; and I laid food before them.

units.leftText: Will they not return to the land of Egypt and be ruled by Assyria because they refused to repent?
units.rightText: They shall not return into the land of Egypt; but the Assyrian shall be their king, because they refused to return to me.

units.leftText: A sword will flash through their cities; it will destroy the bars of their gates and consume them in their own plans.
units.rightText: And the sword shall fall upon their cities, and shall consume their bars, and devour them, because of their own counsels.

units.leftText: My people are bent on turning from Me. Though they call to the Most High, He will by no means exalt them. God’s Love for Israel
units.rightText: And my people are bent on backsliding from me: though they call them to him that is on high, none at all will exalt him.

units.leftText: How could I give you up, O Ephraim? How could I surrender you, O Israel? How could I make you like Admah? How could I treat you like Zeboiim? My heart is turned within Me; My compassion is stirred!
units.rightText: How shall I give thee up, Ephraim? how shall I cast thee off, Israel? how shall I make thee as Admah? how shall I set thee as Zeboiim? my heart is turned within me, my compassions are kindled together.

units.leftText: I will not execute the full fury of My anger; I will not destroy Ephraim again. For I am God and not man — the Holy One among you — and I will not come in wrath.
units.rightText: I will not execute the fierceness of mine anger, I will not return to destroy Ephraim: for I am God, and not man; the Holy One in the midst of thee; and I will not come in wrath.

units.leftText: They will walk after the LORD; He will roar like a lion. When He roars, His children will come trembling from the west.
units.rightText: They shall walk after Jehovah, who will roar like a lion; for he will roar, and the children shall come trembling from the west.

units.leftText: They will come trembling like birds from Egypt and like doves from the land of Assyria. Then I will settle them in their homes, declares the LORD.
units.rightText: They shall come trembling as a bird out of Egypt, and as a dove out of the land of Assyria; and I will make them to dwell in their houses, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: Ephraim surrounds Me with lies, the house of Israel with deceit; but Judah still walks with God and is faithful to the Holy One.
units.rightText: Ephraim compasseth me about with falsehood, and the house of Israel with deceit; but Judah yet ruleth with God, and is faithful with the Holy One.
leftNotes: 11:12 Or and Judah is unruly against God, the faithful Holy One

units.leftText: Ephraim feeds on the wind and pursues the east wind all day long; he multiplies lies and violence; he makes a covenant with Assyria and sends olive oil to Egypt.
units.rightText: Ephraim feedeth on wind, and followeth after the east wind: he continually multiplieth lies and desolation; and they make a covenant with Assyria, and oil is carried into Egypt.
leftNotes: 12:1 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verses 8 and 14

units.leftText: The LORD has a charge to bring against Judah. He will punish Jacob according to his ways and repay him according to his deeds.
units.rightText: Jehovah hath also a controversy with Judah, and will punish Jacob according to his ways; according to his doings will he recompense him.
leftNotes: 12:2 Jacob means he grasps the heel or he deceives.

units.leftText: In the womb he grasped his brother’s heel, and in his vigor he wrestled with God.
units.rightText: In the womb he took his brother by the heel; and in his manhood he had power with God:

units.leftText: Yes, he struggled with the angel and prevailed; he wept and sought His favor; he found Him at Bethel and spoke with Him there —
units.rightText: yea, he had power over the angel, and prevailed; he wept, and made supplication unto him: he found him at Beth-el, and there he spake with us,
leftNotes: 12:4 Or Angel
12:4 LXX and Syriac; MT and there He spoke with us

units.leftText: the LORD God of Hosts, the LORD is His name of renown.
units.rightText: even Jehovah, the God of hosts; Jehovah is his memorial name.

units.leftText: But you must return to your God; maintain love and justice, and always wait on your God.
units.rightText: Therefore turn thou to thy God: keep kindness and justice, and wait for thy God continually.

units.leftText: A merchant loves to defraud with dishonest scales in his hands.
units.rightText: He is a trafficker, the balances of deceit are in his hand: he loveth to oppress.

units.leftText: And Ephraim boasts: “How rich I have become! I have found wealth for myself. In all my labors, they can find in me no iniquity that is sinful.”
units.rightText: And Ephraim said, Surely I am become rich, I have found me wealth: in all my labors they shall find in me no iniquity that were sin.

units.leftText: But I am the LORD your God ever since the land of Egypt. I will again make you dwell in tents, as in the days of the appointed feast.
units.rightText: But I am Jehovah thy God from the land of Egypt; I will yet again make thee to dwell in tents, as in the days of the solemn feast.

units.leftText: I spoke through the prophets and multiplied their visions; I gave parables through the prophets.
units.rightText: I have also spoken unto the prophets, and I have multiplied visions; and by the ministry of the prophets have I used similitudes.

units.leftText: Is there iniquity in Gilead? They will surely come to nothing. Do they sacrifice bulls in Gilgal? Indeed, their altars will be heaps of stones in the furrows of the field.
units.rightText: Is Gilead iniquity? they are altogether false; in Gilgal they sacrifice bullocks; yea, their altars are as heaps in the furrows of the field.

units.leftText: Jacob fled to the land of Aram and Israel worked for a wife — for a wife he tended sheep.
units.rightText: And Jacob fled into the field of Aram, and Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept sheep.
leftNotes: 12:12 That is, northwest Mesopotamia

units.leftText: But by a prophet the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt, and by a prophet he was preserved.
units.rightText: And by a prophet Jehovah brought Israel up out of Egypt, and by a prophet was he preserved.

units.leftText: Ephraim has provoked bitter anger, so his Lord will leave his bloodguilt upon him and repay him for his contempt.
units.rightText: Ephraim hath provoked to anger most bitterly: therefore shall his blood be left upon him, and his reproach shall his Lord return unto him.

units.leftText: When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling; he was exalted in Israel. But he incurred guilt through Baal, and he died.
units.rightText: When Ephraim spake, there was trembling; he exalted himself in Israel; but when he offended in Baal, he died.
leftNotes: 13:1 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verse 12

units.leftText: Now they sin more and more and make for themselves cast images, idols skillfully made from their silver, all of them the work of craftsmen. People say of them, “They offer human sacrifice and kiss the calves!”
units.rightText: And now they sin more and more, and have made them molten images of their silver, even idols according to their own understanding, all of them the work of the craftsmen: they say of them, Let the men that sacrifice kiss the calves.
leftNotes: 13:2 Or “The men who sacrifice kiss the calves!”See 1 Kings 19:18|1KI 19:18*.

units.leftText: Therefore they will be like the morning mist, like the early dew that vanishes, like chaff blown from a threshing floor, like smoke through an open window.
units.rightText: Therefore they shall be as the morning cloud, and as the dew that passeth early away, as the chaff that is driven with the whirlwind out of the threshing-floor, and as the smoke out of the chimney.

units.leftText: Yet I am the LORD your God ever since the land of Egypt; you know no God but Me, for there is no Savior besides Me.
units.rightText: Yet I am Jehovah thy God from the land of Egypt; and thou shalt know no god but me, and besides me there is no saviour.

units.leftText: I knew you in the wilderness, in the land of drought.
units.rightText: I did know thee in the wilderness, in the land of great drought.

units.leftText: When they had pasture, they became satisfied; when they were satisfied, their hearts became proud, and as a result they forgot Me.
units.rightText: According to their pasture, so were they filled; they were filled, and their heart was exalted: therefore have they forgotten me.

units.leftText: So like a lion I will pounce on them; like a leopard I will lurk by the path.
units.rightText: Therefore am I unto them as a lion; as a leopard will I watch by the way;

units.leftText: Like a bear robbed of her cubs I will attack them, and I will tear open their chests. There I will devour them like a lion, like a wild beast tearing them apart. Death and Resurrection (1 Corinthians 15:50–58|1CO 15:50-58*)
units.rightText: I will meet them as a bear that is bereaved of her whelps, and will rend the caul of their heart; and there will I devour them like a lioness; the wild beast shall tear them.

units.leftText: You are destroyed, O Israel, because you are against Me — against your helper.
units.rightText: It is thy destruction, O Israel, that thou art against me, against thy help.

units.leftText: Where is your king now to save you in all your cities, and the rulers to whom you said, “Give me a king and princes”?
units.rightText: Where now is thy king, that he may save thee in all thy cities? and thy judges, of whom thou saidst, Give me a king and princes?
leftNotes: 13:10 Or Shall I be your King now

units.leftText: So in My anger I gave you a king, and in My wrath I took him away.
units.rightText: I have given thee a king in mine anger, and have taken him away in my wrath.

units.leftText: The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is stored up.
units.rightText: The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is laid up in store.

units.leftText: Labor pains come upon him, but he is an unwise son. When the time arrives, he fails to present himself at the opening of the womb.
units.rightText: The sorrows of a travailing woman shall come upon him: he is an unwise son; for it is time he should not tarry in the place of the breaking forth of children.

units.leftText: I will ransom them from the power of Sheol; I will redeem them from Death. Where, O Death, are your plagues? Where, O Sheol, is your sting? Compassion is hidden from My eyes. Judgment on Samaria
units.rightText: I will ransom them from the power of Sheol; I will redeem them from death: O death, where are thy plagues? O Sheol, where is thy destruction? repentance shall be hid from mine eyes.
leftNotes: 13:14 Or Shall I ransom them from the power of Sheol? Shall I redeem them from Death?
13:14 LXX Where, O Death, is your penalty? Where, O Hades, is your sting?Cited in 1 Corinthians 15:55|1CO 15:55*

units.leftText: Although he flourishes among his brothers, an east wind will come — a wind from the LORD rising up from the desert. His fountain will fail, and his spring will run dry. The wind will plunder his treasury of every precious article.
units.rightText: Though he be fruitful among his brethren, an east wind shall come, the breath of Jehovah coming up from the wilderness; and his spring shall become dry, and his fountain shall be dried up: he shall make spoil of the treasure of all goodly vessels.

units.leftText: Samaria will bear her guilt because she has rebelled against her God. They will fall by the sword; their little ones will be dashed to pieces, and their pregnant women ripped open.
units.rightText: Samaria shall bear her guilt; for she hath rebelled against her God: they shall fall by the sword; their infants shall be dashed in pieces, and their women with child shall be ripped up.

units.leftText: Return, O Israel, to the LORD your God, for you have stumbled by your iniquity.
units.rightText: O Israel, return unto Jehovah thy God; for thou hast fallen by thine iniquity.

units.leftText: Bring your confessions and return to the LORD. Say to Him: “Take away all our iniquity and receive us graciously, that we may present the fruit of our lips.
units.rightText: Take with you words, and return unto Jehovah: say unto him, Take away all iniquity, and accept that which is good: so will we render as bullocks the offering of our lips.
leftNotes: 14:2 LXX and Syriac; Hebrew that we may present our lips as sacrificial bulls

units.leftText: Assyria will not save us, nor will we ride on horses. We will never again say, ‘Our gods!’ to the work of our own hands. For in You the fatherless find compassion.” A Promise of God’s Blessing
units.rightText: Assyria shall not save us; we will not ride upon horses; neither will we say any more to the work of our hands, Ye are our gods; for in thee the fatherless findeth mercy.

units.leftText: I will heal their apostasy; I will freely love them, for My anger has turned away from them.
units.rightText: I will heal their backsliding, I will love them freely; for mine anger is turned away from him.

units.leftText: I will be like the dew to Israel; he will blossom like the lily and take root like the cedars of Lebanon.
units.rightText: I will be as the dew unto Israel; he shall blossom as the lily, and cast forth his roots as Lebanon.

units.leftText: His shoots will sprout, and his splendor will be like the olive tree, his fragrance like the cedars of Lebanon.
units.rightText: His branches shall spread, and his beauty shall be as the olive-tree, and his smell as Lebanon.

units.leftText: They will return and dwell in his shade; they will grow grain and blossom like the vine. His renown will be like the wine of Lebanon.
units.rightText: They that dwell under his shadow shall return; they shall revive as the grain, and blossom as the vine: the scent thereof shall be as the wine of Lebanon.

units.leftText: O Ephraim, what have I to do anymore with idols? It is I who answer and watch over him. I am like a flourishing cypress; your fruit comes from Me.
units.rightText: Ephraim shall say, What have I to do any more with idols? I have answered, and will regard him: I am like a green fir-tree; from me is thy fruit found.
leftNotes: 14:8 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel
14:8 Or pine or juniper or fir

units.leftText: Whoever is wise, let him understand these things; whoever is discerning, let him know them. For the ways of the LORD are right, and the righteous walk in them but the rebellious stumble in them.
units.rightText: Who is wise, that he may understand these things? prudent, that he may know them? for the ways of Jehovah are right, and the just shall walk in them; but transgressors shall fall therein.
